title: Architecture Governance — Framework, Board, Contracts, and Compliance

blocks.text: SESSION 1 — Concept · Key Points · Memory Technique. Read, absorb, stop.
1. Concept Explained Simply

Architecture Governance is the constitutional framework for architecture — it establishes how architecture is created, approved, monitored, enforced, and changed across the enterprise. It operates within a hierarchy: **Corporate Governance → Technology Governance → IT Governance → Architecture Governance**. Critical: Architecture Governance is NOT just Phase G. Phase G is one aspect of Architecture Governance, which covers ALL aspects of architecture development and evolution from Preliminary through Phase H.
2a. Key Points — Governance Framework
Six characteristics of governance: **Discipline · Transparency · Independence · Accountability · Responsibility · Fairness**.
Six key governance processes: Policy Management and Take-On · Compliance · Dispensation · Monitoring and Reporting · Business Control · Environment Management.

Three elements of an effective Architecture Governance strategy: A cross-organisational Architecture Board with executive backing · A comprehensive set of Architecture Principles · An Architecture Compliance strategy.
2b. Key Points — The Architecture Board
**Composition**: Cross-organisational; representative of all key stakeholders; typically 4–5 permanent members, no more than 10; needs an executive sponsor from the highest level of the corporation.

**Strategic responsibilities**: Basis for all decision-making regarding architectures · Ensuring consistency between sub-architectures · Establishing targets for re-use · Ensuring flexibility of the EA · Improving architecture maturity.

**Operational responsibilities**: Monitoring and control of Architecture Contracts · Enforcing compliance and granting dispensations · Resolving escalated conflicts · Meeting regularly · Publishing architecture documentation under controlled conditions.

**Architecture Board meeting agenda** — exam-tested items: Minutes of previous meeting · Requests for Change · Dispensations · Compliance Assessments · Dispute Resolution · Architecture Strategy and Direction.
2c. Key Points — Architecture Contracts
**Definition**: Joint agreements between development partners and sponsors on the deliverables, quality, and fitness-for-purpose of an architecture.
Three types — mapped to ADM timing:

rows: Contract between architecting organisation and sponsor — scope, deliverables, resources, approval to proceed
Contract with external development partners (systems integrators, application providers)
End of Phase F / Phase G
Contract between the architecture function and business users who will build and deploy systems

blocks.text: The Standard explicitly states: "The Statement of Architecture Work created in Phase A is effectively an Architecture Contract between the architecting organisation and the sponsor."
2d. Key Points — Architecture Compliance
Five levels of compliance: **Irrelevant · Consistent · Compliant · Conformant · Exceeds**.
Primary goal of a compliance review: Catch errors in the project architecture early to reduce cost and risk of later changes.
**Dispensation**: Granted for a given time period; conditioned on identified criteria; triggers ongoing compliance monitoring.
3. Memory Technique

Governance hierarchy: "Corporate Technology IT Architecture" — each level operates within the one above.

Architecture Board size: 4–5 recommended, maximum 10.

Three Contract types mapped to ADM: Statement of Architecture Work (Phase A) → Design and Development Contract (Phases B–D) → Business Stakeholders Contract (end Phase F / Phase G).

Five compliance levels: Irrelevant → Consistent → Compliant → Conformant → Exceeds.

EXAM TRAP 1 — PHASE G ≠ ARCHITECTURE GOVERNANCE. Phase G (Implementation Governance) is just ONE aspect of Architecture Governance. Architecture Governance covers ALL aspects of architecture development and evolution from the Preliminary Phase through Phase H.

EXAM TRAP 2 — STATEMENT OF ARCHITECTURE WORK IS AN ARCHITECTURE CONTRACT. The Standard explicitly identifies the Statement of Architecture Work as an Architecture Contract. It is BOTH a Phase A deliverable AND the first Architecture Contract in the ADM cycle.
EXAM TRAP 3 — ARCHITECTURE BOARD SIZE IS SPECIFIC. 4–5 permanent members recommended, no more than 10. Do not say "as many as needed." This is directly tested in Part 1.
✋ PAUSE POINT — CHECK BEFORE CONTINUING. Answer from memory before reading Session 2.
1. Phase G is dedicated to Implementation Governance. Is this the same as Architecture Governance?

No. Implementation Governance (Phase G) is just ONE aspect of Architecture Governance. Architecture Governance covers the management and control of ALL aspects of the development and evolution of Enterprise Architectures — from the Preliminary Phase through Phase H.
2. Name the three types of Architecture Contract and when each appears in the ADM.

(1) Statement of Architecture Work — Phase A; contract between architecting organisation and sponsor. (2) Architecture Design and Development Contract — Phases B–D or Preliminary; contract with external development partners. (3) Contract with Business Stakeholders — end of Phase F / Phase G; contract with business users who will build and deploy.
3. What is the recommended Architecture Board size?
4–5 permanent members recommended, with a maximum of 10. The Board must have an executive sponsor from the highest level of the corporation.
SESSION 2 — Real-World Example · How It Works in Practice · Practice Questions · Part 2 Scenario
4. Real-World Example — GlobalTech Dynamics 365

**Architecture Board established in Preliminary Phase**: CTO (executive sponsor), EA Lead, Head of Finance, Head of IT Operations, Head of HR, External Audit representative. Five members — within the 4–5 recommended range.

**Phase A — first Architecture Contract**: Statement of Architecture Work approved by CTO and Architecture Board = the first Architecture Contract. Defines scope (Finance and HR migration), deliverables, timeline (18 months), constraints (Australian data residency, $4.2M budget), and Architecture Principles governing all decisions.

**Phases B–D — Design and Development Contract**: GlobalTech engages a cloud architecture consultancy for Phase D. Architecture Design and Development Contract drawn up — defines scope (Technology Architecture only), conformance requirements (all designs align with GlobalTech's Architecture Principles), deliverables, time window, and escalation process.

**Phase H — Architecture Board monthly agenda**: Requests for Change (AI cash flow feature — incremental, approved via change management) · Dispensations (Procurement integration 90-day dispensation — formally closed once migrated to API Management) · Compliance Assessments (Wave 2 HR project initiation — reviewed and approved to proceed) · Dispute Resolution (Finance vs HR data ownership dispute — Board directs working party to resolve within 30 days).
5. How It Actually Works in Practice

REALITY CHECK: ARCHITECTURE GOVERNANCE WITHOUT EXECUTIVE SPONSORSHIP IS FICTION. The Architecture Board needs not just a sponsor but an active champion willing to say no to business units seeking shortcuts. If the CTO routinely overrides Architecture Board decisions, the governance framework collapses within months.

REALITY CHECK: COMPLIANCE REVIEWS ARE MOST VALUABLE WHEN HELD EARLY. The primary goal is to catch errors when they are cheap to fix — at project initiation and initial design. Reviews held just before go-live find problems that are impossibly expensive to correct.
6. Part 1 Practice Questions
Q1. Which best describes the relationship between Phase G and Architecture Governance?

items: A) Phase G and Architecture Governance are the same thing
B) Phase G is just one aspect of Architecture Governance — Architecture Governance covers all aspects of architecture development and evolution ✓
C) Architecture Governance is a subset of Phase G
D) Phase G replaces Architecture Governance during the delivery phase

blocks.text: Answer: B — the Standard explicitly states this. Frequently tested.
Q2. The Statement of Architecture Work is explicitly identified by the TOGAF Standard as which type of governance document?
Answer: C — the Standard states it is "effectively an Architecture Contract between the architecting organisation and the sponsor."
Q3. The recommended permanent membership size for an Architecture Board is:

items: A) One or two senior executives only
B) As many representatives as needed
C) Four or five members, no more than ten ✓

blocks.text: Answer: C — directly stated in the Standard. Tested in Part 1.
7. Part 2 Scenario Question (Exam-Authentic Format)

SCENARIO: Wave 2 is in delivery. The Head of HR raises two concerns with the CTO: (1) the Architecture Board rejected the Self-Service HR module's dispensation request — the Head of HR believes the Board is "too rigid" and wants the CTO to overrule it; (2) a new HR analytics vendor offers a platform integrating directly with Dynamics 365 HR, bypassing Synapse Analytics entirely — the Head of HR wants to adopt it without an Architecture Compliance review.

rows: Support the Head of HR on both points. Architecture Governance should be pragmatic and the HR analytics platform is a business decision. Fundamentally wrong — CTO overruling the Board destroys governance authority; adopting a vendor without compliance review bypasses the governance framework entirely.

Uphold both Architecture Board decisions. CTO overruling the Board undermines governance; the HR analytics platform requires compliance review. Correct in outcome but doesn't identify the formal mechanism — the Dispute Resolution process — that the Head of HR can use to escalate the dispensation decision.

Advise the CTO: (1) the formal escalation mechanism for the dispensation is the Architecture Board's Dispute Resolution process — not CTO override; (2) the HR analytics platform requires Architecture Compliance review before any adoption decision — the review will determine whether dispensation is appropriate, the architecture needs updating, or the platform should be rejected. Best answer.

Convene an emergency Architecture Board meeting to give the Head of HR's concerns equal weight to the Board's previous decisions. Partially recognises the Board as the decision-making body, but "equal weight" mischaracterises governance — the Board's decisions stand until formally overturned through the Board's own process.
